subject: Design & Technology
label: Public edition
assessment_verbatim: F: safe-working observation.  S: constructed product + evaluation (data drop).

sources.note: Current main bytes match the accepted unchanged source; workbook not redistributed.
W3 16–20 Nov; W4 23–27 Nov. One lesson weekly per line; no day or slot inferred.

external_sources.title: HSE: Health and safety checklist for classrooms
external_sources.supports: The ordinary classroom checklist excludes specialist D&T; staff use activity-appropriate risk controls and local procedures.

external_sources.title: Science Buddies: Build the Best Paper Bridge
external_sources.supports: Folding a sheet into a channel can change how it resists bending. The local dimensions, light block test and stop rules are authored classroom choices; no strength result is assumed.

evidence.description: The learner’s actual folded card model, a labelled photo/work reference, build checks, one change or next step and accurate physical-support record.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Supported: Supported: ask an adult to steady the card.
routes.Independent: Independent: fold, form and check the model.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: explain how the shape fits the plan.

vocab.definition: A small version of an idea.
One flat part of the card.
The line made by a fold.
Something that holds an object up.

cases.text: Find your plan and your flat marked card.
cases.fact: The model begins with the agreed plan.
cases.next_step: Check 20 cm by 8 cm and both fold lines.
cases.staff_note: Use the accepted Week 2 work. If absent, provide a spare pre-marked blank and record that preparation as adult support, not pupil marking-out evidence.

cases.text: Check lines are 2 cm and 6 cm from the same long edge.
cases.fact: The middle panel should be 4 cm wide.
cases.next_step: Pause and ask if a mark does not fit the plan.
cases.staff_note: Do not guess a new fold. Both lines use the same reference edge.

cases.text: Fold the first outer panel up along its line.
cases.fact: The fold follows the marked line.
cases.next_step: Press gently on a flat desk with adult support if needed.
cases.staff_note: Use suitable card that folds by hand. No scoring knife, cutting tool or sharp creasing tool.

cases.text: Fold the other outer panel up. Keep the middle flat.
cases.fact: The two sides form a channel shape.
cases.next_step: Check that each side is about 2 cm high.
cases.staff_note: Adult may steady or start a crease; record who did what. Do not claim independence when the adult made the fold.

cases.text: Set two stable supports 10 cm apart. Centre the model across them.
cases.fact: A centred 20 cm model has 5 cm at each end on a support.
cases.next_step: Ask staff to check the supports and fit.
cases.staff_note: Staff set equal-height supports on a tray. This is a fit check with no added load. Use only pre-torn tape if an agreed join needs securing.

cases.text: Label the model, record your work and store it for next week.
cases.fact: The actual model is evidence of building.
cases.next_step: Keep a photo or work reference and note any help.
cases.staff_note: No strength result is claimed. Store without crushing folds; a blank worksheet is not evidence of a built model.

Purpose and success checks
How can I turn my marked card into a model?
I can follow my plan to form the model. I can make and check two clear folds. I can record my work and the help I used.
LAUNCH-DT-W3-E1: The learner’s actual folded card model, a labelled photo/work reference, build checks, one change or next step and accurate physical-support record.
Before pupils arrive

Retrieve Week 2 plans and labelled 20 by 8 cm card blanks. Staff prepare spare marked blanks, soft foldable card, rulers, pencils, mats, pre-torn tape and storage. Staff set equal-height stable supports with a measured 10 cm gap on a tray. Trial the hand-folding task under local risk controls.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.

Access and practice
Supported: ask an adult to steady the card. Independent: fold, form and check the model. Aspire: explain how the shape fits the plan.

Follow A–F. Check marks first, model one crease on spare card, then let pupils form their own channel. Adults record physical help. Use a fit check over the 10 cm gap only. For an absent pupil, record supplied marking as catch-up support and focus on today’s building objective.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Use hand-foldable card with clean edges and no staples. Learners fold by hand; adults can steady the card. No pupil cutting, sharp scoring tools, blades, hot glue, power tools or load tests. Supports sit on a stable low desk/tray; no standing on a model or testing with hands or body weight.
Assessment and feedback

A 20 by 8 cm blank folded at 2 cm and 6 cm gives a 4 cm base and two 2 cm sides. A centred 20 cm length across a 10 cm gap rests 5 cm on each support. Check actual folds and fit. Capture the model, not just a plan. Record adult-started folds or a supplied pre-marked blank. No load, strength or award completion result is inferred.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Speaking listening and writing

Explain the next making step, listen to a practical instruction and describe a checked or corrected fold. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Model and hinge

Check the card: 20 cm long and 8 cm wide. Find lines 2 cm and 6 cm from one long edge. Fold each outer panel up along its line. Keep the middle 4 cm panel flat. Place it across a 10 cm gap between supports. Centre it: 5 cm rests on each support.

B. Check the 2 cm and 6 cm lines from the same reference edge. Ask the adult whether the fold can be corrected or a spare blank is needed; record the help and change. A hides rather than resolves the mismatch; C introduces unplanned cutting. Re-model a fold on scrap card if needed.
Individual evidence key

A 20 by 8 cm blank folded at 2 cm and 6 cm gives a 4 cm base and two 2 cm sides. A centred 20 cm length across a 10 cm gap rests 5 cm on each support. Check actual folds and fit. Capture the model, not just a plan. Record adult-started folds or a supplied pre-marked blank. No load, strength or award completion result is inferred.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Use the accepted Week 2 work. If absent, provide a spare pre-marked blank and record that preparation as adult support, not pupil marking-out evidence.
Card B: Do not guess a new fold. Both lines use the same reference edge.
Card C: Use suitable card that folds by hand. No scoring knife, cutting tool or sharp creasing tool.
Card D: Adult may steady or start a crease; record who did what. Do not claim independence when the adult made the fold.
Card E: Staff set equal-height supports on a tray. This is a fit check with no added load. Use only pre-torn tape if an agreed join needs securing.
Card F: No strength result is claimed. Store without crushing folds; a blank worksheet is not evidence of a built model.
Common misunderstandings

A drawn plan is not a built model. A fit check without a load does not show strength. Correcting a fold or asking for help is part of making. A neat appearance alone does not prove that the model will hold a load.
Teaching boundary

Use hand-foldable card with clean edges and no staples. Learners fold by hand; adults can steady the card. No pupil cutting, sharp scoring tools, blades, hot glue, power tools or load tests. Supports sit on a stable low desk/tray; no standing on a model or testing with hands or body weight.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
